key_insight: Replacing the SAE encoder with per-sample sparse coding makes learned concepts far more consistent across runs, improving reproducibility of dictionary discovery.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more reliable way to analyze foundation model representations when stable, cross-seed interpretability matters for downstream scientific or engineering workflows.
method: Use sparse coding instead of a single linear encoder for each sample.
Learn a sparse dictionary while optimizing coefficients per instance, not via one forward pass.
Measure consistency of recovered dictionaries and coefficients across random seeds.
evidence_signal: Across 16 synthetic settings and four vision/language benchmarks, ConSDL achieved near-perfect recovery and improved cross-seed dictionary consistency by 17.6% and coefficient consistency by 35.9% over the average of six SAE baselines.
watch_item: Per-sample sparse optimization is more computationally demanding than standard encoder-based SAEs, so runtime and scalability should be checked in large-scale deployments.
paper_title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
